items.markdown:
`In 2026, Thailand is facing an intense climate phenomenon characterized as a "Super El Niño" which emerged in May and is projected to peak between November 2026 and January 2027` . The prolonged weather event brings severe threats of historic droughts, extreme temperatures exceeding 45°C, and major risks to agricultural output and water supplies.[](https://www.facebook.com/TheNationThailand/posts/thailand-faces-a-high-risk-of-entering-a-prolonged-el-ni%C3%B1o-phase-from-june-2026-/1439372668216063/) [[1]](https://www.facebook.com/TheNationThailand/posts/thailand-faces-a-high-risk-of-entering-a-prolonged-el-ni%C3%B1o-phase-from-june-2026-/1439372668216063/)[[2]](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40066641)[[3]](https://en.vietnamplus.vn/thailand-strengthens-response-to-risk-of-prolonged-el-nino-post344739.vnp)

Impact and Expectations

Forecasters from the [ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre](https://asmc.asean.org/asmc-el-nino/) and the [Bangkok Post](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/3271826/el-ni%C3%B1o-set-to-continue-all-year) project temperatures to consistently run 1.5°C to 2.0°C above normal. Regions in the Northeast, East, and South of Thailand are receiving below-normal rainfall, placing a heavy strain on the country's electricity and water supply systems.[](https://www.facebook.com/TheNationThailand/posts/thailand-faces-a-high-risk-of-entering-a-prolonged-el-ni%C3%B1o-phase-from-june-2026-/1439372668216063/) [[1]](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/3271826/el-ni%C3%B1o-set-to-continue-all-year)

- **Agriculture:** The combination of prolonged heat and drought puts immense pressure on rice yields, risking losses of millions of tons across Southeast Asia.
- **Environment:** Severe dry conditions have heightened the risk of wildfires, transboundary haze, and deteriorating PM2.5 air pollution.[](https://www.facebook.com/TheNationThailand/posts/thailand-faces-a-high-risk-of-entering-a-prolonged-el-ni%C3%B1o-phase-from-june-2026-/1439372668216063/) [[1]](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/jun/05/el-nino-asia-unpredictable-extreme-weather-climate-change-crisis)[[2]](https://www.bnr.nl/nieuws/internationaal/10604173/oorlog-en-godzilla-achtige-el-nino-hebben-ingrijpende-gevolgen-voor-zuidoost-azie)[[3]](https://gistda.or.th/news_view.php?n_id=9130&lang=EN)

Government Response Because of the severity of the projections, the Thai government has placed the country under maximum surveillance. Agencies are accelerating climate adaptation measures, compiling spatial drought-risk data, promoting conservation, and helping farmers shift to low-water-demand crops.[](https://gistda.or.th/news_view.php?n_id=9130&lang=EN) For a closer look at how this extreme weather event is threatening the country's agriculture, economy, and everyday life:![Thumbnail van gerelateerde video](https://encrypted-tbn2.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcQy6TF947dFbUcp1buVvWI8uBmW96d3ufA72Cy2as7w4GQPdsT4)
